ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $OB$ is a ray inside $\angle AOC$, $OM$ is a ray inside $\angle AOB$, and $ON$ is a ray inside $\angle BOC$. In Figure 2, if $\angle AOC=140^\circ$, $\angle AOM=\angle NOC=\frac{1}{4}\angle AOB$, and $\angle BOM:\angle BON=3:2$, what is the degree measure of $\angle MON$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle AOM=\angle NOC=x$, thus $\angle AOB=4x$,\\
$\therefore \angle BOM=\angle AOB-\angle AOM=3x$,\\
$\because \angle BOM\colon \angle BON=3\colon 2$,\\
$\therefore \angle BON=2x$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOC=\angle AOB+\angle BON+\angle NOC=7x=140^\circ$,\\
$\therefore x=20^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle MON=\angle BOM+\angle BON=5x=\boxed{100^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In Figure 2 on the right side of the attached figure, all rays start from point O. Observing in the order from one side to the other side of the large angle ∠AOC, the rays are successively OA, OM, OB, ON, OC. Therefore ∠AOC is divided into four adjacent parts: ∠AOM, ∠MOB, ∠BON, ∠NOC; and ∠MON is obtained by adding ∠MOB and ∠BON. Reasoning: Let ∠AOM=∠NOC=x. The problem statement gives ∠AOM=1/4∠AOB, so ∠AOB=4x. Since ∠AOB is composed of ∠AOM and ∠MOB, ∠BOM=∠AOB-∠AOM=4x-x=3x. Also because ∠BOM:∠BON=3:2, and ∠BOM=3x, so ∠BON=2x. By adding adjacent angles in Figure 2, ∠AOC=∠AOB+∠BON+∠NOC=4x+2x+x=7x. It is known that ∠AOC=140°, so 7x=140°, solving gives x=20°. Therefore ∠MON=∠BOM+∠BON=3x+2x=5x=100°.
